title: Progressive decommission + compatibility-adapter playbook for legacy model versions
creator: Asha Patel
description: This ticket captures a structured, low-friction decommission workflow for old model versions with two complementary controls: (1) an automated 'compatibility adapter' shim to preserve commonly used inputs/outputs for a limited window, and (2) a progressive notification + pinning safeguard system that prevents silent breakage for production customers. Goal: reduce customer surprise, minimize manual migrations, and provide measurable signal into cost/quality trade-offs for model retirement decisions.
background: We routinely onboard new model checkpoints and publish performance profiles. Historically, retirements have caused more support tickets and last-minute rollbacks than expected — often because customers had pinned model names, used undocumented output shapes, or relied on small deterministic differences. A compatibility adapter is a narrow, runtime-level transformation layer (SDK + routing) that can emulate legacy behaviour for a bounded time while nudging customers to migrate. This document defines the lifecycle, acceptance criteria, communication cadence, telemetry checks, and rollback procedures.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Compatibility adapter implemented as a configurable runtime/SDK plugin and can be toggled per-customer. 2) In-console banners, email templates, and API warnings exist for 90/60/30/14/7/1 day stages. 3) Pinning safeguards: if a customer pins a version scheduled for decommission, an automated review task is created and the pin is labeled 'legacy-pinned'. 4) Migration guide generator produces a per-customer delta table (latency, token-cost, quality delta on canonical eval set). 5) Telemetry dashboard surfaces migration progress and customer health metrics. 6) Hand-off runbook for CS/SE with rollback steps is published.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 sprints): design API surface for compatibility adapter (SDK hooks + routing flag), add admin toggle in Console, and author notification templates. Phase 2 (2 sprints): build adapter for common gaps (structured JSON field renames, legacy function calling shapes, tokenization quirks), instrument telemetry, and create migration report generator. Phase 3 (1 sprint): run pilot with 10 customers on non-critical models, collect feedback and iterate. Phase 4: full rollout and formal decommission calendar integration (calendar-driven state machine that promotes notices and eventually disables adapter).
compatibility_adapter_spec:
- Scope: small, well-scoped transforms only (field renames, legacy role mappings, common post-processing tokens). Not meant for full behavioral parity.
- Implementation: SDK-level transformation + an optional runtime routing layer for requests via adapter. Adapter has versioned rulesets stored in ConfigStore and applied per-customer.
- Config contract: adapter_id, transform_ruleset_version, expiry_date, customer_allowlist.
- Failure mode: if adapter throws, request falls back to explicit model variant fallback policy and logs error.
- Monitoring: adapter hit-rate, transform-error-rate, 95th latency delta compared to native path.
notification_cadence: Standard cadence: Announcement (90 days), Reminder (60 days), Migration-assist offer (30 days), Final warn (14 days), Urgent final (7 days), Day-before (1 day). Channels: console banner (sticky), email to billing/SRE/engineering contacts, in-console migration assistant modal, and webhook to customer Slack if configured. Each message includes: reason, recommended replacement, expected delta table link, action buttons (Start automated migration | Request manual assistance | Pin and request exception).
pinning_safeguards:
- When a customer pins a model that appears on an active decommission calendar, the Console shows an inline modal describing the retirement date and risk.
- If they confirm pinning, system creates an internal review ticket assigned to the on-call Solutions Engineer and labels the customer 'legacy-pinned'.
- Pinning for 'critical' tier customers requires explicit CS approval (two-step).
- Logs: pin_event, customer_ack_timestamp, reviewer_id, exception_expiry_date.
migration_guide_generator: Generates a per-customer guide that contains: 1) Baseline metrics (latency, cost per request, tokenization diffs), 2) Quality deltas on canonical prompt sets, 3) Suggested prompt edits and parameter mappings, 4) Automated test harness commands (redwood-eval run --customer <id> --prompts <path>), 5) Rollout plan (canary percentages, traffic ramp), 6) Known incompatibilities requiring manual intervention.
telemetry_checks: Minimum telemetry: pre/post latency (p50/p95), tokens per request, top error classes, adapter error-rate, regression_alert_count (automated eval fails), customer-satisfaction signals (support tickets created). Alert thresholds: p95 increase > 20% or regression_alert_count >= 3 triggers auto-pause of adapter rollout and creates incident in Ops.
communications: Linked artifacts: Confluence decommission checklist (confluence.redwood.com/pages/DECOM-templates), customer-facing migration docs (drive.redwood.com/migration-library), PR reference for adapter: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pulls/1849. Templates are stored in the Console content manager and include 'short', 'detailed', and 'exec' variants. Example subject line: '[Action Required] Model vX.XX will be retired on 2025-06-15 — migration tools available'.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: customers rely on undocumented behavior that adapter cannot emulate leading to broken flows. Mitigation: conservative adapter scope, pilot cohort, automatic rollback for regressions, manual CS-assisted migrations, and extended grace periods for enterprise contracts. Risk: operational overhead from review tasks — mitigate with triage automation and prioritization heuristics.
notes:
- The adapter is explicitly time-bounded (configurable expiry).
- Keep public deprecation schedule updated on status.redwood.com.
- Consider adding 'minimal emulation' flags to SDKs for customers who need just tokenization compatibility.
- This playbook should be used for model families where exit cost > threshold (to be defined by Product).
support_hand_off: CS playbook checklist: 1) Confirm customer has migration report, 2) Offer 1:1 migration session, 3) If requested, create 'migration-assist' engagement with SE, 4) Track outcome tags (migrated | exception-granted | rolled-back).
postmortem_criteria: If >5% of pilot cohort required manual rollback or an enterprise customer suffers > 3% revenue-impact due to migration, open a formal postmortem within 72 hours. Postmortem report should include root cause, protective measures, and timeline for remediation.
open_questions: 1) How long is the default adapter grace period (30/60/90 days)? 2) What is the threshold for 'critical' tier requiring CS approval? 3) Should the adapter ruleset be editable by SEs via Console or manually via PRs?
